profilePeriod: 2021–2025 vice presidency and 2024 presidential platform; latest public remarks checked through September 2026.

sources.title: A New Way Forward: economic opportunity platform
sources.evidence: Private enterprise, housing supply incentives, consumer protection, strategic manufacturing investment, Buy American procurement and opposition to blanket tariffs; responsible AI and biotechnology investment.

sources.title: Where Harris stands on ten policy issues
sources.evidence: Reproductive rights, tougher border enforcement, climate action and changed position on fracking; platform reflects 2024 rather than every 2019 promise.

sources.title: Harris makes a capitalist pitch
sources.evidence: She publicly described a pragmatic, pro-business economy supporting middle-class opportunity and home ownership.

sources.title: Harris at Tribal Nations Summit
sources.evidence: Supports tribal self-determination and federal investment; condemns coerced assimilation and suppression of Native languages.

sources.title: Democratic convention speech transcript
sources.evidence: Supports voting-rights legislation, nationwide reproductive freedom, alliance leadership and immigration reform combining a citizenship path with border security.

sources.title: September campaign remarks
sources.evidence: Calls for Senate checks on executive abuses and participation in midterm elections.

sources.title: Harris condemns White House press exclusions
sources.evidence: Condemns withdrawal of press credentials and supports scrutiny of executive action.

sources.title: ACLU assessment of Harris criminal-justice record
sources.evidence: Identifies criminal-justice reform commitments alongside prosecutorial experience; advocacy demands in this document must not be mistaken for Harris commitments.

sources.title: ACLU assessment of Harris surveillance record
sources.evidence: Documents surveillance and privacy concerns; executive law-enforcement powers coexist with constitutional constraints. ACLU proposed reforms are not all Harris policy.

sources.title: Drug Policy Action Harris fact sheet
sources.evidence: Documents sponsorship of marijuana reform and movement toward legalization; does not establish support for legalizing all drugs.

sources.title: Gun ownership and safety restrictions
sources.evidence: Harris supports personal gun ownership and the Second Amendment alongside an assault-weapons ban and additional safety restrictions.

sources.title: Position on decriminalizing prostitution
sources.evidence: Supported decriminalization in 2019; campaign declined to clarify position in 2024.

sources.title: Harris meets Zelenskyy
sources.evidence: Supports Ukraine against Russian aggression and NATO security; emphasizes sovereignty and territorial integrity.

sources.title: Alliances, military strength and opposition to Iran war
sources.evidence: Opposes Iran war of choice while explicitly valuing US military strength, NATO expansion, international norms, human-rights influence and reliable alliances.

sources.title: Harris rejects starting Iran war
sources.evidence: ABC Australia report and video: at Austrian World Summit, Harris says she would not have started Iran war.

sources.title: Federal Reserve independence
sources.evidence: Reuters reports support for Federal Reserve independence from presidential decisions.

sources.title: Baptist faith and religious pluralism
sources.evidence: Baptist faith, Hindu family influences and Jewish spouse; religious faith informs social justice rather than a uniform state creed.

sources.title: Faith and reproductive choice
sources.evidence: Argues faith and reproductive freedom coexist and government should not dictate reproductive decisions.

sources.title: Harris LGBTQ rights remarks
sources.evidence: Frames LGBTQ equality as a fundamental freedom.

sources.title: London speech on AI
sources.evidence: Supports AI innovation with rigorous safety testing and safeguards against discrimination and other harms.

sources.title: Harris chairs National Space Council
sources.evidence: Promotes space exploration, Earth-science benefits and sustainable human presence in space through international partnerships.

sources.title: Penguin Random House: The Truths We Hold
sources.evidence: Publisher confirms Kamala Harris authorship and original publication date; bestselling political memoir.

sources.title: Intrínseca: As verdades que nos movem
sources.evidence: Brazilian publisher verifies translated title and political substance covering justice, immigration, inequality, health care and national security.

facts: 2023 tribal speech affirms self-determination and federal partnership.
2024 national reproductive and voting-rights protections imply federal rights floors.
estrutura.tension: Federation and local administration remain legitimate; national civil-rights standards do not imply one police force or presidential supremacy over courts.

facts: 2024 supports statutory voting-rights protections.
2026 calls for Senate oversight and condemns excluding journalists.
representacao.tension: Representative constitutional democracy is not government by experts, permanent popular assemblies or unrestricted plebiscites.

facts: Prosecutorial background coexists with reform and marijuana legalization.
2024 defends gun ownership alongside assault-weapons limits.
poder.tension: Public safety and legal investigative powers coexist with due process; neither police abolition nor blanket surveillance immunity follows.

facts: 2024 combines citizenship pathways and border enforcement.
Rejects cultural erasure and values a plural national identity.
imigracao.tension: Border restrictions concern enforcement and capacity, not a demand for ethnic uniformity; multiculturalism does not mean borderlessness.

facts: 2024 supports armed defense of Ukraine.
2026 opposes Iran war while retaining strong military and allied security.
diplomacia.tension: Deterrence and defense are supported; preventive regime-change war is not. Diplomatic preference is not abolition of armed forces.

facts: 2024 defends Ukrainian sovereignty.
2026 values US global influence and NATO but condemns war of choice.
intervencao.tension: Allied projection and sanctions are compatible with rejecting territorial conquest and unilateral aggression; not neutral isolationism.

facts: 2024 explicitly endorses capitalism and home ownership.
Platform supports social protection, unions, affordable health care and competition.
economia.tension: Redistribution and public services coexist with private productive property; no general nationalization agenda established.

facts: 2024 supports strategic industrial subsidies and consumer safeguards.
Supports independent Federal Reserve.
controle.tension: Regulated competition rather than command planning; national economic coordination does not mean presidential control of interest rates.

facts: 2024 promotes domestic manufacturing and Buy American.
Rejects indiscriminate tariffs and backs productive international commercial relationships.
comercio.tension: Targeted industrial protection alongside integration; neither autarky nor unconditional free trade.

facts: 2024 Baptist faith remains personally significant.
Explicitly defends reproductive choice without requiring abandonment of faith.
religiao.tension: Faith may inspire personal moral service while laws protect people of different faiths or none; no state religion.

facts: 2024 prioritizes reproductive autonomy and LGBTQ civil rights.
Sex-work policy has a recorded unresolved shift.
moral.tension: Progressive civil rights do not establish enthusiasm for every lifestyle or unrestricted drug commerce; sex-work answer reflects real policy tension.

facts: 2023 backs AI benefits with safety standards and sustainable space exploration.
2024 supports advanced industry while retaining environmental protections.
tecnologia.tension: Neither anti-industrial naturalism nor unregulated transhumanist acceleration; therapeutic biotechnology differs from selecting embryos for appearance.

limitations: The survey is a reasoned persona simulation, not 240 quotations. Brazilian institutions are interpreted through equivalent US governance choices; no claim Harris stated Brazilian policies.
Preserved explicit period: 2021–2025 vice presidency and 2024 presidential platform; latest public remarks checked through September 2026. Search cutoff 2026-10-01.

No direct positions were verified on embryo intelligence editing, brain enhancement, cultivated meat, municipal tax allocation or all local-service arrangements. Those answers are qualified inferences from innovation, civil rights and constitutional governance; N is reserved for genuine competing considerations.
2024 campaign promises supersede incompatible 2019 proposals. Later 2026 remarks strengthen evidence against elective regime-change war without negating alliance commitments.
ACLU and Drug Policy Action are advocacy organizations; distinguish their descriptions of her record from their requests to a potential administration.
Searches did not establish a new comprehensive 2026 platform; do not invent one.
